name: Divine Hand
body:
A divine hand is a chosen individual trained from a young age to be an instrument of their deity against those who are apostate to their religion. They can be used as assassins, problem solvers, saboteurs, or negotiators. Whatever the mission, they answer the call of their deity.

Alignment: A divine hand must be within one step of their deity or religion.

Class Features
Seek the Apostate (Sp)

At 1st level, a divine hand can use detect chaos, detect evil, detect good, or detect law as spell-like abilities. They can only use the spells that detect alignments that are opposite from their deity or religion. For example if their deity is Lawful Good, they can use detect chaos or detect evil. They can only use one of the spells at any given time.

If the divine hand’s deity or religion is neutral on either axis, they gain both spells that deal with that axis. For example, a divine hand of a Neutral Evil cult would have access to detect chaos, detect good, and detect law. A divine hand of a Neutral deity or religion, though rare, gains access to all four.

This ability replaces the get the job done ability gained at 1st level.

Blessed Zeal (Su)

At 2nd level, a divine hand is instilled with a powerful zeal anytime they are faced with those that are in conflict with their religion. On any round that a divine hand delivers an attack or uses an offensive ability against a creature whose alignment differs on both axes, they gain a +2 sacred bonus on Will saves against that opponent’s abilities or spells, as well as the benefit of Diehard feat until the end of their next turn. For example, if the divine hand of a Chaotic Good deity faces an opponent who is Neutral Evil or Lawful Evil, they would get the benefit, but they would not get the benefit from a Chaotic Neutral enemy. If the divine hand attacks or uses offensive abilities against multiple qualifying enemies, they gain the Will bonus against all of them but they only gain the effects of Diehard once. If the divine hand already has Diehard or later gains Diehard, They treat their Constitution score as double to determine if they may continue to act while this effect is active. This ability replaces the slayer talent gained at 2nd level.

Undying Instrument (Su)

At 6th level, mortal wounds cannot stop the divine hand from dispensing their proscribed justice. When blessed zeal is active, they are not staggered while benefiting from the Diehard feat at negative hit points. Additionally, during such rounds, they do not need to make stabilization checks, though they are not considered stabilized. This ability replaces the slayer talent gained at 6th level.

Divine Smite (Su)

At 10th level, any creature that the divine hand has triggered blessed zeal against takes 2d6 extra damage from the divine hand once per round. This damage is considered divine damage and is not subject to damage reduction or resistance. However, this damage does not stack with other effects that deal extra damage based on alignment, like a paladin’s smite or an anarchic weapon. The damage is added anytime the divine hand deals damage with a weapon, natural attack, spell or ability. This ability replaces the advanced slayer talent gained at 10th level.
